data.title: Second Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques Quran and Sunnah Competition for West Africa Concludes in Nouakchott in Presence of Mauritanian President
data.content:
Nouakchott, November 20, 2026, SPA -- The Ministry of Islamic Affairs, Dawah and Guidance held yesterday a closing ceremony in Nouakchott, attended by Islamic Republic of Mauritania President Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani, for the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques Competition for the Memorization of the Holy Quran and the Prophetic Sunnah for West African Countries, which brought together it its second edition 160 participants from 16 countries over four days.
    In an address delivered on his behalf by Deputy Minister Dr. Awad Al-Anazi, Minister of Islamic Affairs, Dawah and Guidance Sheikh Dr. Abdullatif Al Alsheikh affirmed Saudi Arabia's commitment to serving the Holy Quran and Sunnah under the patronage of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and the oversight of His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince and Prime Minister, highlighting the King Fahd Glorious Quran Printing Complex's annual production of 20 million copies and thanking President El Ghazouani for attending.
    Mauritanian Minister of Islamic Affairs and Original Education Sid'Elhaje Ould Dah, Saudi Ambassador to Mauritania Dr. Abdulaziz Al-Raqabi, and Secretary-General of the Mauritanian Scholars Association Sheikh Ould Saleh underscored the deep fraternal ties between the two nations and praised the Kingdom's efforts in promoting moderation and supporting Quranic scholarship.
    The ceremony concluded with President El Ghazouani and officials honoring the winners across the competition categories, who received cash prizes totaling SAR1,140,000.
    -- SPA
